title: The Big Yawning: Pathological Yawning as a Symptom of Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorders
case_prompt: A 67-year-old woman presented with a 7-day history of progressive left-sided limb ataxia and hypesthesia. On admission, she exhibited frequent yawning (>3/min) in salve-like episodes (>8 yawns), without fatigue or boredom, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. There were no cranial nerve deficits. Brain MRI showed moderate leukoaraiosis but no inflammatory lesions. A signal enhancement extending to the lower medulla was noted on a coregistered spinal MRI. Subsequent cervical MRI revealed a longitudinal lesion of the cervical cord extending over more than three vertebral segments. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed a lymphocytic pleocytosis (7 cells/µL) without elevated protein, and CSF-restricted oligoclonal IgG bands were present. Visual evoked potentials were normal bilaterally.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Other systemic autoimmune, infectious, vascular, neoplastic, or paraneoplastic disorders were excluded — “There was no evidence for alternative diagnoses such as other systemic autoimmune, infective, vascular, neoplastic, or paraneoplastic disease.”  
2. Common neurologic causes of pathological yawning were considered but lacked supporting features — “Differential diagnoses for pathological yawning include ischemic stroke (in the upper brainstem, insula, or caudate nucleus …), autonomic epileptic seizures, parkinsonism, intracranial hypertension due to infections or brain tumors, and side effects of medications (e.g., serotonin reuptake inhibitors and apomorphine) . We could not find such factors in the present case as an alternative explanation.”  
3. Multiple sclerosis was deemed unlikely given the rarity of yawning in MS and the pattern of longitudinally extensive myelitis — “Pathological yawning is not frequently observed in other chronic inflammatory central nervous system diseases apart from a single case report in multiple sclerosis.”  
4. Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder was supported by longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis and serologic evidence — “The diagnostic criteria for a NMOSD were fulfilled: positive test for AQP4-IgG and acute myelitis.”
